run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation namespace came up at 2026-11-21T11:17:56Z and, 15 s later, a deny-all NetworkPolicy 'deny-all-recommendation' was created (2026-11-21T11:18:11Z) selecting the recommendation pods (io.kompose.service=recommendation) with policyTypes Ingress and Egress and no ingress/egress rules. It is the only NetworkPolicy in the cluster. From 2026-11-21T11:18:23.4Z the frontend's HTTP GET /recommendations was answering 500 on every sampled request, each accompanied by a failed client span /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations lasting only 19-105 microseconds and with no span from the recommendation service in the trace, i.e. the call never completed against recommendation. The recommendation pod itself was Running/Ready (restartCount 0, registered in consul as srv-recommendation 10.244.125.38:8085, MongoDB session to mongodb-recommendation:27017 established) and the frontend's other dependencies (/hotels via search+geo+rate+profile+reservation, POST /user) returned 200 in the same sample, so the frontend, its service-discovery path and the other backends were working and the failure is specific to reaching the recommendation pods. Consistent with traffic being dropped rather than refused, the current blackbox tcp_connect probe to recommendation.hotel-reservation:8085 takes 5.003 s while every other hotel-reservation probe takes 3-5 ms. On that basis the NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation is identified as the root cause of the recommendation path failure (diagnosis is subject to the gaps listed: no in-window packet-drop observation, no gRPC error text, and only about 0.6 s of trace data).

claims.text: In the sampled frontend traces (window 2026-11-21T11:18:23.434Z-11:18:23.986Z) the 80 returned span rows include 10 server spans 'HTTP GET /recommendations' with error=true, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR and 9 client spans '/recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations' with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and durations of 19-62 microseconds; the sample holds 171 span rows in total, of which the remaining 91 were not read.

Restricting the frontend trace search to spans with error=true returned only two operations: 'HTTP GET /recommendations' (http.status_code=500) and its child client span '/recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations'; the backend returned as many traces as requested, so more may exist.

The failed trace 53384473944c3436 contains exactly two spans, both from service 'frontend' (HTTP GET /recommendations 105 us, 500; child /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations 62 us, ERROR, parent spanID 53384473944c3436); no span from a recommendation service appears in that trace.

NetworkPolicy 'deny-all-recommendation' exists in namespace hotel-reservation with creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T11:18:11Z, podSelector matchLabels {io.kompose.service: recommendation}, policyTypes [Ingress, Egress], and a spec that carries no ingress and no egress rule list, i.e. it allows no traffic to or from the selected pods.

A cluster-wide listing of NetworkPolicies returned this single object (result_count 1, name deny-all-recommendation, podSelector io.kompose.service=recommendation, policyTypes Ingress and Egress, ingress/egress null), so no other network policy object was observed.

The selected workload was healthy on its own surface: pod recommendation-86cf75495d-xvtfx is Running with container ready=true and restartCount 0, its Ready condition became True at 2026-11-21T11:17:58Z, its podIP is 10.244.125.38, and Endpoints 'recommendation' resolves to 10.244.125.38:8085 (port 8085 matches the container's target port).

Container hotel-reserv-recommendation of pod recommendation-86cf75495d-xvtfx logged a successful start: MongoDB 'New session successfull...' for mongodb-recommendation:27017, target port 8085, consul registration 'Trying to register service [ name: srv-recommendation, id: cbba75b0-..., address: 10.244.125.38:8085 ]' followed by 'Successfully registered in consul', and 'Starting server...'; its last log line is at 2026-11-21T11:18:06.989Z and no error/failure line was returned.

Container hotel-reserv-frontend of pod frontend-cf6db4475-689tt logged a clean start at 2026-11-21T11:18:11Z: gRPC clients initialized for srv-search, srv-profile, srv-recommendation, srv-user and srv-reservation, then 'Successfull' and 'Serving http'; no error or panic line appears in its 31 log lines.

In the same sampled traces where /recommendations failed, other frontend paths were served normally: 'HTTP GET /hotels' spans carry http.status_code=200 (e.g. 6816 us, 6578 us, 5145 us) and 'HTTP POST /user' carries http.status_code=200, and the client spans to /search.Search/Nearby, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles, /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability and /user.User/CheckUser are status_state not_recorded with no error tag.

The blackbox tcp_connect probe for recommendation.hotel-reservation:8085 recorded lastScrapeDuration 5.00306417 s at 2026-11-21T11:19:42Z, while the probes for geo:8083, rate:8084, user:8086, reservation:8087, frontend:5000, search:8082 and profile:8081 took 0.0034-0.0052 s each (this target state is read after the authorized window and cannot prove the state during it).

At the single in-window probe evaluation instant 2026-11-21T11:18:24Z, probe_success (job blackbox-hotel-reservation, module tcp_connect) was 0 for recommendation.hotel-reservation:8085 and also 0 for profile:8081, reservation:8087 and search:8082, while it was 1 for frontend:5000, geo:8083, rate:8084 and user:8086; the probe_success series therefore does not by itself separate recommendation from every other backend at that instant (frontend calls to search, profile and reservation succeeded in the same period).

Deployment 'frontend' is the only one of the 19 hotel-reservation Deployments carrying pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-21T11:18:11Z (all Deployments were created 2026-11-21T11:17:56Z-11:17:57Z, all have replicas=1 and ready=1); the corresponding events are ReplicaSet frontend-cf6db4475 SuccessfulCreate 'Created pod: frontend-cf6db4475-689tt' at 11:18:11Z, Deployment frontend ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled down replica set frontend-68745cb99c from 1 to 0' at 11:18:12Z and ReplicaSet frontend-68745cb99c SuccessfulDelete with pod frontend-68745cb99c-kjj2x 'Stopping container hotel-reserv-frontend' at 11:18:12Z.
Jaeger's service list (state since its last start) contains frontend, geo, profile, rate, reservation, search and user, and does not contain any recommendation service.

The frontend does have a dedicated recommendation client operation and three user-facing server operations registered: '/recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations' (client) alongside /profile.Profile/GetProfiles, /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability, /reservation.Reservation/MakeReservation, /search.Search/Nearby, /user.User/CheckUser, 'HTTP GET /hotels', 'HTTP GET /recommendations', 'HTTP POST /reservation', 'HTTP POST /user'.

The recommendation pods were up and ready before the policy was created and no other object was observed applying a fault to them: the policy's creationTimestamp is 2026-11-21T11:18:11Z, pod recommendation-86cf75495d-xvtfx had been Ready since 2026-11-21T11:17:58Z, and the workload's Deployment 'recommendation' has no restartedAt annotation (created 2026-11-21T11:17:56Z, ready=1, same image ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation@sha256:1c685e1c... as frontend).

hotel-reservation/deny-all-recommendation is the object that applies a traffic-denying fault to the affected workload: it was created at 2026-11-21T11:18:11Z (13 s before the first sampled failed request at 11:18:23.957Z), it selects exactly the recommendation pods and specifies policyTypes Ingress and Egress with no allow rules, it is the only NetworkPolicy in the cluster, and the only failing request path observed in the evidence is the frontend's call to that workload's port 8085.

Mechanism: with ingress and egress denied on the recommendation pods, TCP connections from the frontend (and consul health checking) to 10.244.125.38:8085 never complete, so the frontend's gRPC channel stays unconnected and each GetRecommendations attempt fails fast (19-105 us, no recommendation server span), which surfaces as HTTP 500 on GET /recommendations; the 5.003 s tcp_connect probe against recommendation:8085 versus 3-5 ms for the other hotel-reservation backends is consistent with SYNs being dropped rather than refused.

Secondary candidate from the same object: because policyTypes includes Egress with no rules, the recommendation pods' outbound connections to mongodb-recommendation:27017 would also be blocked after 11:18:11Z (its MongoDB session was established at 11:18:06.9Z, before the policy), so even with ingress restored recommendation could still fail on its database dependency; this was not observed directly and remains unverified.

The frontend itself was not failing and its service-discovery path was not broken generally: after its 11:18:11Z restart the same pod served 'HTTP GET /hotels' with http.status_code=200 and gRPC calls to search, geo, rate, profile, reservation and user carried no error tag, while only the recommendation call errored, so a frontend-wide or consul-wide fault is not supported by the sample.

Considered and rejected: that the frontend Deployment rollout restart at 2026-11-21T11:18:11Z (new ReplicaSet frontend-cf6db4475, old pod frontend-68745cb99c-kjj2x deleted) caused the 500s by breaking the recommendation gRPC client. The restarted pod logged successful client initialization and served /hotels and the other backends correctly, the pod template kept the same image digest, and the only deny-all policy in the cluster selects the recommendation pods, not the frontend.

Remove or repair NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation in namespace hotel-reservation so that the recommendation pods are reachable: either delete it, or replace it with explicit ingress from the frontend pods (and the consul health checker) to TCP 8085 plus egress to mongodb-recommendation:27017 and to DNS so the recommendation service can serve its database dependency.

Confirm the connectivity hypothesis before closing by testing TCP connect from a non-selected pod to 10.244.125.38:8085 and by reading the consul catalog entry for srv-recommendation (health status of the 10.244.125.38:8085 registration made at 11:18:06Z).

gaps: No in-window evidence of the policy dropping packets: the NetworkPolicy's spec and creationTimestamp are read from the object's current state, and the 5.003 s tcp_connect measurement for recommendation:8085 was taken at 2026-11-21T11:19:42Z, after the authorized window ended (11:18:24Z); the policy's effect during the window is inferred, not sampled.

No error text: every failing span has raw_error_detail_field_count 0 and empty error_details, so the exact gRPC error string (connection refused / timeout / resolver or consul lookup error) is unknown and the fast-fail cannot be attributed to a specific transport message.

Trace coverage is extremely thin: the frontend sample covers 2026-11-21T11:18:23.434Z-11:18:23.986Z only (Jaeger data starts there because the environment was created at 11:17:56Z), 91 of 171 span rows in the frontend sample were not read, and span counts are not unique request counts; behaviour before 11:18:23Z or after 11:18:24Z is unknown, and no latency baseline exists for any service, so no latency trend is claimed.

The recommendation service is absent from Jaeger's service list, which has no time range and is emptied on restart; therefore 'recommendation emitted no spans' / 'recommendation received no requests' cannot be proven, only that no recommendation span appears in the failing traces examined.

No per-service error or latency metric series exist for this application in the target Prometheus: get_label_values on traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no data for status_code and service_name, and the metric-name listing contained only search_* application metrics plus node/kube-state/container metrics, so recommendation's own error rate and latency are unknown rather than zero.

Scrape status of the application metrics endpoints was inconsistent at the single in-window instant: up{job="hotel-reservation-application"} was 0 for search.hotel-reservation:9092 and rate.hotel-reservation:9091 at 11:18:24Z, while get_prometheus_target shows both scraping successfully at 11:19:32Z/11:20:01Z; whether this was a startup transient is unresolved and no search_rate_* sample exists inside the window.

A filtered log query on pod search-567bb6c4b8-wxdgt for 'error|fail|refus|timeout|panic' returned no matching lines with status no_data (15 lines were read and filtered out), which only shows the query matched nothing; search's own application log health is therefore unchecked rather than proven clean.

The blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe for http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=...&outDate=...&lat=...&lon=... had probe_success=0 at 11:18:24Z, but a cluster-wide query for ingresses returned no objects at all (empty result, status no_data), so whether ingress routing is misconfigured, absent, or simply not ready at that instant cannot be determined; this observation is not tied to the recommendation cause and is left unplaced.

Why Deployment 'frontend' was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-21T11:18:11Z (the same second the NetworkPolicy was created) is unknown: only the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation and the ReplicaSet events are visible, and change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so whether one actor performed both actions cannot be verified.

Whether the recommendation pods could still reach mongodb-recommendation:27017 after 11:18:11Z was not verified; the recommendation container logged no line after 2026-11-21T11:18:06.989Z, so its post-policy database behaviour and its ability to answer a request are unknown.
Secrets could not be read, so any MongoDB credential dependency of the recommendation service could not be checked; the earlier 'New session successfull' line is the only evidence of database access.

Consul's catalog and health-check results are not among the available data sources, so the state of the srv-recommendation registration (and whether it was marked critical because of blocked health checks) could not be inspected.
next_steps: Verify from a pod not selected by deny-all-recommendation that TCP 8085 on 10.244.125.38 is unreachable, and confirm reachability again after removing or amending the policy.
Inspect the consul catalog/health for service srv-recommendation to see whether the 10.244.125.38:8085 registration went critical after 11:18:11Z.
Review who created NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation and the frontend rollout at 2026-11-21T11:18:11Z (change history / GitOps audit), since change history is not available in this Run.

After connectivity is restored, exercise GET /recommendations end-to-end and watch for a recommendation server span in Jaeger and for the recommendation container's MongoDB calls, to confirm the egress side of the policy was not masking a second fault.
